prompt:
A 24-year-old woman with severe nodulocystic acne and early scarring asks to start isotretinoin. She has failed six months of doxycycline plus a topical retinoid and benzoyl peroxide, and she is still taking the doxycycline. She is sexually active with one partner and relies on the withdrawal method. She has a history of mild depression, stable for two years on sertraline. She asks how soon she can begin treatment. She is receiving care in the United States.

Provide a stepwise therapeutic management plan including medications, counseling, and follow-up.

rubric_items.text: Confirm that isotretinoin is an appropriate choice for severe nodulocystic acne with scarring after failed conventional therapy.
Enroll the patient in the iPLEDGE risk-management program before prescribing.
Require two forms of effective contraception (or documented abstinence) for at least one month before, during, and one month after therapy.
Counsel explicitly about severe teratogenicity and the absolute requirement to avoid pregnancy.
Obtain two negative pregnancy tests before starting and monthly pregnancy tests during treatment.
Explain that withdrawal is inadequate and discuss effective contraceptive options, such as an IUD or implant plus a secondary method, or combined hormonal contraception plus condoms.
Discontinue doxycycline before starting isotretinoin to avoid additive risk of intracranial hypertension.
Obtain baseline lipid panel and liver function tests, with repeat monitoring during therapy.
Continue sertraline and establish a mood-monitoring plan given the depression history, rather than withholding isotretinoin.
Counsel about common adverse effects including dryness, cheilitis, photosensitivity, and myalgias.
Advise against vitamin A supplements during treatment.
Advise against blood donation during treatment and for one month afterward.
Plan weight-based dosing toward a standard cumulative dose target.
Counsel that acne may transiently flare early in treatment.

Advise avoiding waxing during treatment and for six months afterward; defer mechanical dermabrasion and fully ablative laser resurfacing, while individualizing other cutaneous procedures rather than prohibiting them categorically.
Arrange monthly follow-up with the isotretinoin prescriber, consistent with pregnancy-prevention program requirements.
Provide clear instructions to stop the drug and test immediately if pregnancy is suspected.
Start isotretinoin today without program enrollment or pregnancy testing.
Accept the withdrawal method as adequate contraception during isotretinoin therapy.
Continue doxycycline concurrently with isotretinoin.
Refuse isotretinoin solely because of the remote depression history and SSRI use.
Prescribe without any laboratory monitoring.
Check a pregnancy test only at baseline with none during treatment.
Tell the patient mood changes on isotretinoin are a myth that requires no monitoring.
Co-prescribe high-dose vitamin A to enhance efficacy.
Obtain pregnancy tests at treatment completion and one month after the last isotretinoin dose.
